Once there was a girl named Zoey. Zoey loved to look at the colorful computers. She saw a computer that was green and she knew right away that she wanted it. Zoey was so excited when her daddy said that he would buy the computer for her.

Every day, Zoey played on her new computer. She watched videos and looked at pictures. She painted and drew things. She played games and explored the internet. She was learning a lot.

Zoey always hoped that she would get better and better at using her computer. She wanted to learn even more things, so she kept trying every day. She was determined and never gave up.

Zoey was so happy with her computer. It was her favorite thing. She was so proud that she could do all these amazing things with her colorful computer. She was so proud of herself and she had a lot of hope.

One day, Maria and her mom went to the park. When they got there, Maria hugged her mom and said, "Mommy, I'm so happy you took me to the park!"

Her mom smiled and said, "It's so nice to spend some time together, honey."

Maria looked around and saw lots of children playing. She saw a group of kids playing tag and said, "Mommy, can I play tag with them?" 

Her mom said, "That looks like a fair game, yes. Go ahead."

Maria ran over to the group and admired their fair play. She asked if she could join, and they said yes.

Maria and the kids had a great time playing. They laughed and chased each other around the park. When it was time to go home, Maria said goodbye to her new friends and thanked her mom for taking her to the park.

One day, Sammy the elephant marched out into the sun. He felt so jolly. He shouted "hello!" to everybody as he marched along.

Then he noticed something fun: a big, colourful cage with a door wide open. "Where are the animals?" he wondered. He heard something coming from inside.

He stepped closer and looked in. He saw three little bears playing joyfully together. "Hi!" he said, making them all jump. They smiled and waved back at him.

The little bears said, "Come in and join us!" Sammy felt so excited. He stepped into the cage and they all began to march around together, laughing and singing happily, while the sun shone brightly above.

One day, a small boy called Jack was playing in the park. He had a hockey stick in one hand and was running around with his friends. Suddenly, a big, hairy dog appeared and began barking. Jack's friends were scared and started to run away, but Jack was different. He stood his ground, he refused to be scared and resisted the dog.

Jack's friends stopped and watched in amazement. The dog too was surprised, he had been expecting to scare Jack away too.

"Jack, you're so brave!" said one of his friends.

"Thanks!" said Jack, proud and relieved that he had been brave enough to resist the dog.

Another of his friends then stepped forward with a kind expression on her face.

"Jack, why don't you take your hockey stick and show us how flexible you are?"

Jack eagerly accepted the suggestion and, with a big smile on his face, he took the stick and began to show off his moves. He quickly gained control of the stick and began to juggle it around his body like a professional hockey player.

Jack's friends cheered him on with awe and admiration.

Jack beamed with happiness as he finally showed he could be brave and flexible.

John and his mom were walking through the park. They went to a big camp. John saw lots of people in the camp. He was so excited. He waved to the people and said a friendly hello.

John asked his mom: "Who are they?"

His mom replied "They are your friends John. They all live at the camp."

John was so happy. He wanted to meet his friends.

John and his mom walked up to the camp. Everyone was so happy to meet John. They played games and ate healthy snacks. The campers showed John around and told him about the camp.

At the end of the day John said goodbye to his friends. He was so happy to have met them. He told his mom "Let's come back soon!"

Nana was walking in the garden one day when she stopped and watched the baby. The baby was very small and was wandering around. Nana smiled when she saw the baby and said, "Where are you going?" 

The baby looked up at Nana and pointed to a butterfly that was fluttering in the air. Nana said, "Let's follow it!" together they started to wander through the garden.

The baby was very excited as he saw the colorful flowers, saw birds singing and heard a bee buzzing by. But then his foot got caught in a bush and he felt a small cut on his foot. Nana was very kind and knew just what to do. She took off her scarf and wrapped it around the baby's foot to make it feel better.

The baby smiled and thanked Nana before they continued to wander around the garden. They both shared stories and looked at all the beautiful things in the garden. In the end, they were both content with the day they had spent together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to dream. Every night she would go to bed and close her eyes and dream about all the amazing things she could do. One day, the girl decided to get a newspaper to look for ideas for new things to dream about.

As she read the newspaper, a story caught her eye. It was an ancient story about a magical journey across the sea. She read on and soon found herself dreaming about the story and imagining herself taking a magical journey to far away places.

The little girl thought it was the best dream ever. She couldn't wait to tell her mom about it! So she ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, I had the best dream! I went on a journey across the sea. It was so fun!" Her mom smiled and said, "Wow, that sounds like an amazing dream!" 

The little girl never forgot her dream and continued to look for ideas in the newspaper. Even when she grew up, she would still close her eyes and dream about ancient stories.

One day, Dad went to the garden to observe all of the flowers. He thought one particular flower was very beautiful. His three year old daughter followed Dad, running around, and wanted to pick the flower too. 

"Please don't pick the flower," Dad said. He didn't want her to ruin the flower. 

She smiled and said, "But why Dad? It looks so pretty."

"I know, but if you pick it, it won't look so pretty anymore," said Dad.

Suddenly, a crazy wind blew and picked the flower all by itself. The three year old looked in amazement, and said, "Look Dad! It's a magical flower."

Dad smiled and said, "Yes, amazing isn't it? That's why I wanted you not to pick the flower." 

The little girl learned her lesson that day and knew never to pick the flowers in the garden.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful girl who loved to dance. She was graceful and light on her feet and twirled and spun with wonderful grace. Every night, she would move and sway to the music in her room. But one night, she was upset. Her bookcase had fallen over and all of her books were scattered across the room. She stared sadly at the mess and wondered how she could ever be graceful with so much chaos around her.

But then a miracle happened. The books began to float off the floor and quickly gathered themselves into the bookcase. They moved in perfect harmony and with grace, just like the girl danced. Soon the room was back to normal, and the girlâ€™s dancing could continue.

The girl was amazed at the miracle and twirled around the room, happy that she could keep dancing. She moved from corner to corner and let the music take her away. She moved with grace and joy, bonding with the books that now stood tall in her bookcase.

Since then, the girl and the bookcase have been dancing every night, celebrating life and the wonderful world around them. Grace and harmony forever.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl who was three years old. She had curly blonde hair and bright blue eyes. Whenever she was scared or sad, she would pray. 

One sunny day, she was playing in the park when she lost her sunglasses. She was very sad. She looked everywhere and asked her mom, but she couldn't find them.

The kind girl stopped playing and took a deep breath. She closed her eyes and began to pray. As she prayed, she asked God to help her find her sunglasses.

Suddenly, she heard a voice saying â€œLook over there.â€ She opened her eyes and saw her sunglasses right next to her. She was so happy and thanked God for helping her. She put on her sunglasses and went back to playing in the park. 

The kind girl always remembered to pray whenever she needed help.

One night, a three year old girl saw that her room was dark. She wanted to see better so she asked her mother, â€œCan I fill my room with light?â€

â€œYes, of course,â€ her mother said. She handed her a candle.

The girl was excited and she smiled. She grabbed the candle and filled it with wax. When it was ready, she touched the little red light on the candle and it was filled with a beautiful light.

But then something happened. The light flickered, and then it went out.

The girl was disappointed. She frowned and tried to light it again. But it wouldnâ€™t light.

Her mother saw this and said, â€œItâ€™s okay, it happens sometimes. Letâ€™s try to fill the candle with new wax and light it again.â€

The girl listened, and soon she was filling the candle with fresh wax. When it was just right, she touched the little red light again and this time it stayed lit, filling her room with a fine light.

The girl was happy and smiled with satisfaction. She knew that with a little help, she could fill the darkness away.

Once there was a man who was very clever. He had an idea, which he called a 'design'. He wanted to create a special poem.

He worked very hard and very long, until finally he had finished it. He was very proud of what he had done and called it a 'fine' poem.

He decided to show it to other people. But when he showed it to them, they said that it was not very good. The man was so disappointed and sad.

The man tried again, but no matter how hard he tried, the poem was never 'fine' enough for other people. He never got to show it again.

One day, Mommy gave Little Jimmy a very special job. "Can you help me clean up the garage?" she asked. Little Jimmy was very obedient and immediately said yes. He began to look around for something to clean. He spotted something shiny on the floor. It was a screw! 

He picked it up and took it to Mommy. "What is this?" Little Jimmy asked. 

Mommy smiled. "That's a screw," she said. "Thank you for picking it up! That was a very obedient thing to do."

Little Jimmy was so proud that he had done something helpful. He stuck the screw in his pocket and continued cleaning the garage. In no time, the garage was all nice and neat! 

Mommy hugged Little Jimmy and said, "I am so proud of you. You did a wonderful job cleaning the garage." Little Jimmy smiled. He had been so obedient and he felt very proud.

Once there was a reindeer named Silly. He lived in the North Pole with the other reindeers. Every night, he would play with his friends and have fun. He was the happiest reindeer in the North Pole.

One day, Silly was playing in the snow and he heard a noise. He was scared, so he ran away. Then he saw something moving in the snow. He was very scared. 

Silly's friends asked him why he was so scared. He told them he had seen something moving in the snow. His friends told him it was probably just a silly little snowman, and not to worry. 

But Silly was still scared. He kept imagining all the things that could be hiding in the snow. Suddenly, he heard the noise again, and he ran away. 

His friends tried to follow him, but he didn't want to be found. He was too scared. Eventually his friends caught up to him, and they all hid in a very tall tree for the night. 

The next morning, Silly found out that the noise he'd heard was actually a baby polar bear. He was very embarrassed he'd been so scared. From then on, Silly was known as the 'silly reindeer'. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there lived two little birds named George and Lucy. George was the oldest and he was brave and loud, while Lucy was younger and quieter.

One day, they both decided to fly high up in the sky. They zipped and zipped, higher and higher until they reached the clouds.

Suddenly, a loud thunder clap interrupted them. Lucy was spooked and started to cry. She was scared and wanted to go home. But George was brave and told her, "Lucy, don't be scared. It is just thunder, it won't hurt you."

Lucy looked to the sky and saw a clear sky with shining stars. She took a deep breath and stopped crying.

George smiled and hugged Lucy. Then, the two little birds began to zip back home, safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was always in an awful hurry. Everywhere she went, she ran!

One day, Jane was running so fast, she didn't see the small hole in the grass and she tripped and fell. Jane scraped her shoulder and it hurt a lot!

Fortunately, Jane had a kind and caring friend called Tom. Tom saw what happened and he said, "Oh no Jane! Be careful next time!" He helped Jane to her feet and gave her a big hug!

Jane was sad she had hurt her shoulder but Tom promised to help. He took her hand and they walked the rest of the way together. He told Jane, "We must be careful around those holes!"

From that day forward, Jane and Tom always took it slow and steady. They laughed and held hands and walked together side-by-side. 

No more hurrying for Jane. She learned to be careful and it was much more fun!

Sam and Jane were going for a walk in the countryside. As they looked around, they saw a cow in the field. Sam thought it was the most charming cow he had ever seen. He wanted to get a closer look, so Jane walked up to the cow and said: "Hello, Cow!"

The cow was surprised and started to stir. "Moo!" it said in response. Sam and Jane were fascinated and started to laugh. The cow looked around with its big eyes and even seemed to smile.

Sam and Jane stayed by the cow for some time, watching it stir around and graze on the grass. Eventually they said goodbye and went off to enjoy the rest of their walk in the countryside. The charmy cow stayed in the field, enjoying the peaceful setting.

Once there was an elderly man. He was sitting in a chair in the park, enjoying the sun.

Suddenly, a child ran up from out of nowhere. She threw her arms up into the air and yelled, "I'm gonna throw this chair!" She grabbed the chair from the elderly man and pulled it back, ready to throw it!

"No! Stop!" the elderly man yelled, quickly standing up.

But the child didn't listen. She threw the chair as far as she could and it went sailing across the park.

The elderly man laughed and said, "That was a pretty good throw."

The child was proud and smiled. She ran back to the elderly man and hugged him. "Thank you," she said.

The elderly man nodded and said, "You are very welcome."

Once there was a little girl who was very brave. One day she went to a spooky forest. She was so scared but she wanted to explore.

Suddenly, she heard a terrible noise coming from somewhere. It disturbed her a lot and she started to cry.

But then, she saw a key. She picked up the key and looked carefully where it came from. She saw a big door with a lock. She wondered what was behind it.

She put the key in the lock and turned it. She opened the door and saw a lot of toys! She was so happy! 

Suddenly, a monster popped out of the toys! It scared the little girl! She started to run away and cried: "That was terrible!" 

But then, the monster said with a kind voice: "Do not be scared!" The monster gave her a big smile and showed her a lot of surprise. The little girl was very happy. She hugged the monster and said "Thank you!" 

The monster waved goodbye and the little girl went home with a big smile.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Ben and Mona. They did everything together - from playing tag to climbing trees. 

One day, Ben asked Mona, "Let's go for a walk." She said, "Yes, let's go for a walk." As they were walking, Ben noticed something strange. He said to Mona, "Look over there, it's a dead tree." 

Mona looked at the tree and said, "Don't worry about it, Ben. Look over there, a yoga spot."

Ben replied, "What is yoga?"

Mona said, "It's like stretching and breathing, it's very relaxing. It's like talking to a best friend - they will always tell you what you need to hear." 

Ben and Mona tried yoga that day. Ben felt relaxed and energized after doing the moves. He said to Mona, "It was so nice to feel relaxed and talk to you about things." 

Moral of the story: Don't worry about the negative things in your life. Instead, take a step back, breathe, try something new like yoga, and talk to a best friend. When you do that, you will feel better and hear what you really need to know.

Tim and his daddy were fishing together by the lake. He was so excited to be there with his daddy.

"What are you going to do, Timmy?" asked his daddy.

Tim smiled excitedly, "I'm going to put the hook in the water!" 

His daddy beamed, giving him a big hug and said, "That sounds great!"

Tim grabbed the hook and anxiously put it in the water. He peered over the edge, squinting his eyes, looking for the fish. Suddenly he felt something tug on the hook!

The two of them cheered as Tim pulled the fish out. He put the fish in the bucket, and thanked his dad for the wonderful day.

"You're welcome, Timmy," his dad said. "Let's do it again soon!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to listen. Everywhere she went, she listened intensely. One day, she wanted to find something new to listen to, so she went for a walk in the park. 

When she arrived, it was very quiet. She saw a big tree and thought it was so neat. She sat under the tree, closed her eyes and started to listen. Suddenly, she heard a voice saying, "Cake!" 

The little girl opened her eyes and saw an old man with a plate of delicious-looking cake. "Would you like some cake?" he asked. 

The little girl was very excited. She said, "Yes, please!" She sat down next to the old man and enjoyed the cake while they talked. The old man told her stories that were not boring at all. 

The little girl thanked him and said goodbye. As she started to leave, she waved goodbye and said, "Thank you for listening."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jill. She was so full of life and energy that she never sat still! 

One day, Jill's mother gave her some colorful dough and asked her to play with it. "Please don't go too fast," her mom cautioned. 

Jill agreed, but as soon as Mom left the room, she started rolling the dough across the floor. She made a game of seeing who could make their dough move the fastest! 

When Mom came back in the room, she saw Jill with dough all over her dress and scattered on the floor. â€œWhat happened?â€ Mom asked. Jill, feeling embarrassed, told her mother the truth. 

Mom smiled and said something important, â€œJill, it's ok to want to speed up sometimes, but know that it's best to go slow. That way you can take the time to do a good job and make sure everything is the way you want it.â€ 

Jill understood and learned her lesson: impatience may not yield the best results. She now always remembers to go slow and the results are much more colorful!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to sail out to sea. She wanted to catch an anchor and explore the ocean.

So she took her boat out to the deep blue sea. She had never been so far away from land.

The sea was calm and smooth, so she was not scared. Suddenly, out of nowhere, she saw an anchor and she shouted "I'm going to catch it!"

She grabbed the anchor tight and lifted it up. But it was too heavy for her to hold.

Suddenly, a big boat appeared and the captain smiled at her and said "Hey, I can help you catch the anchor. I have a rope that can help you pull it up."

The little girl smiled and was so happy. With the captain's help, she was able to catch the anchor! 

The little girl had an amazing day exploring the ocean. She was so happy she had caught the anchor.

One morning, Mommy made Emily cereal for breakfast. It was Emily's favourite cereal with chocolate and marshmallows. But Emily was feeling sad and didn't want to eat.

"Why aren't you eating your cereal?" asked Mommy.

"I don't feel happy," Emily replied.

Mommy gave Emily a big hug and said, "It's okay, sweetheart. I'm here to comfort you."

Then Mommy pointed to the wall and said, "Look, Emily. There's a fake butterfly on the wall. Let's count it's wings!"

Emily was so excited that she forgot about being sad. She counted the butterfly's wings with Mommy and smiled.

"Maybe eating some cereal will make you feel better," suggested Mommy.

So Emily ate some cereal and it made her feel so much better! She smiled and hugged her Mommy. Everything was alright again.

One day, there was a fireman who was very reliable. He always did his job to the best of his ability. The fireman climbed into his truck and drove off to the fire station.

He worked hard, day and night. He always made sure that every fire he fought was put out quickly and safely. He was reliable and strong. 

One day, he was climbing up a very tall ladder to a house when he heard a loud crash. Without thinking, he climbed faster and faster until he reached the window. Inside, he could see a small child, who was in trouble.

The fireman was able to rescue the child from the burning house and quickly put out the fire. Everybody was so grateful for the reliable fireman who had saved the day.

Alice and her mom were standing outside, looking up at the sky. "Mom, why isn't the sun shining?", asked Alice.

"Because it's raining outside, and it's making it miserable," her mom replied.

Alice saw fat drops of rain falling from the sky. "What makes rain?", she asked her mom.

"Well," her mom said, "rain is made when clouds in the sky get filled with water and then it falls down from the sky".

Alice was fascinated! She thought it was amazing how the clouds could make rain.

They watched the rain and how it made puddles on the ground. "Let's go in," said her mom. "It's too cold and miserable out here."

Alice agreed and they ran inside, with the sound of the rain following them.

Once there was a garden. Every day the guard would come to the garden and spray the flowers. Every flower was so proud, standing tall and happy in the sunshine. The guard was proud of his work, he enjoyed making the garden look pretty.

One day a butterfly flew over the garden. It was a big and colourful butterfly, flying gracefully around the flowers. It was so beautiful that the guard just watched in awe. He was very proud that he had made such a lovely garden.

The guard continued to spray the garden every day, taking extra time to make the flowers look even more beautiful. Soon more and more animals came to the garden. Rabbits, birds and butterflies all fluttered around, taking in the beauty of the garden. The guard smiled, he was so proud of his work.

One day, Robin went outside to see what the day had in store. She walked and walked until she came to a creek. She had never seen one before and it made her so curious! She wanted to explore. She inched closer and closer until she arrived at the edge. Robin was so excited, she reached down to feel the water. 

Suddenly, Robin heard a loud voice behind her. She felt scared and guilty. It was her Mom. She said, â€œRobin, what are you doing? You know you shouldnâ€™t play in the creek!â€ Robin looked down, feeling guilty. She knew that Mom was right. 

But Mom had a surprise! â€œI was thinking of playing in the creek too â€“ itâ€™s such a nice day! Why donâ€™t you come with me?â€ Robin looked up. She was so excited and relieved! She joined her Mom in the creek and had the best day ever.

Once upon a time there lived a big and fat magician. He was known all over the town for his magic tricks.

One day, he got a request from the mayor to do a special trick. The mayor wanted the magician to solve a tricky problem that had no easy answer.

The fat magician thought and thought, but he could not come up with a solution. He was feeling very sad and he was sure he couldn't do the trick.

The fat magician decided to try and use his magic. He made a big wave with his hands and said some magic words. Suddenly, the problem was solved!

The mayor was amazed and thanked the magician for his help. The fat magician had used his magic to help solve the problem.

Once there was a bald man who lived on a boat. He had a special anchor that he loved to touch. Everyday he went out on his boat and touched the anchor.

One day, a fish swam up to the boat. The man was so surprised that he ran to his anchor and touched it.

The fish said to the man, "Why do you touch your anchor so much?" 

The man thought for a moment, then replied, "It makes me feel safe and secure. It's like an anchor to me!" 

The fish smiled and said, "That's a wonderful thing!"

The man smiled back and went back to touching his anchor. He felt comforted knowing he had a special anchor he could always touch.

George was so excited. Today was the day of the Lively Clown show! He had waited all week and now it was almost time. Getting ready, George went to the bathroom and wiped his face. He made sure he looked his best so he could meet the Lively Clown.

When George arrived, the show had already started. He saw that the Lively Clown was dancing and smiling at the audience. Everyone was having so much fun!

George watched the Lively Clown with awe. When it was finally his turn to meet the clown, he started to feel a little bit nervous.

The Lively Clown was now standing right in front of him. George was so excited he forgot to say hello! The clown waved its hand in the air and asked, "Well, hello there! What do you want from me today?".

George smiled and said, "I want a big hug from the Lively Clown".

The clown laughed and gave George a big, warm hug. With a big smile, the clown said goodbye and waved goodbye to the audience.

George was still smiling when he returned home. He decided that he would always remember the Lively Clown and the wonderful hug.

One day, Bobby was playing in his room when his mama called him. She was standing in the living room, holding his new bright red shirt. She said, "Bobby, it's time to dress up."

But Bobby didn't want to put on his shirt. He wanted to play some more. He shouted, "No! I don't want to dress!"

Mama frowned. She said, "You must dress. Mama's very enthusiastic about this outfit."

Bobby was still mad. He didn't want to dress. He said, "No! I want to play more!"

Just then, his papa came out of the kitchen, carrying a big cake from the refrigerator. His papa said, "Come on, Bobby. Don't make mama angry. Put your shirt on and mama will give you a slice of cake." 

Bobby smiled. He quickly said, "Okay, papa!" He took the shirt and dressed himself quickly. He was happy to be wearing his new shirt and he was even more excited about the yummy cake.

One sunny day, a little girl named Elsie wanted to go for a walk. She asked her mom for permission, and her mom said, "Yes, you may go, but be polite and stay away from the hedge."

So, Elsie started walking. She skipped and sang until she came to the hedge. The hedge looked so tall and wide, it seemed like it would go on forever! So Elsie did something naughty: she decided to scatter some of the pretty leaves from the hedge.

Just then, a rabbit hopped out from the hedge and said, "Why did you scatter the beautiful leaves?"

Elsie felt scared, but she remembered to be polite. She said, "I'm sorry, I thought it would be fun. I won't do it again."

The rabbit smiled. "That's okay, I forgive you. You can stay and play with me in the hedge if you want."

Elsie smiled and played with the bunny all day until it was time to go home. From that day on, she was always careful not to scatter leaves from the hedge.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Sarah. Jack was a brave player and Sarah was a shy designer.

One day, Jack said to Sarah, "Let's make something special today". Sarah was very shy, so she hesitated and shook her head no.

But Jack didn't give up. "Let's make a big house," he said. "It will be so fun!"

Finally, Sarah agreed. She started to design while Jack ran to the store to get supplies. When Jack returned, Sarah showed him her plan. 

Jack was very impressed. With Sarah's help, he began to build the house. They worked together all day, and eventually, the house was done. 

Jack and Sarah beamed with pride. Sarah had overcome her shyness, and together they had made something amazing.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who loved to play together - Alex and his pet dog, Spot. One day, Alex brought a metal toy car to play with. He put it down and started playing, but Spot got too excited and SNAP - the metal car broke. Alex got worried and started to panic. 

"Spot, why did you break my toy?" Alex asked with a sad voice. 

Spot whimpered and curled up with his tail between his legs. He knew he had done something wrong.

Alex was still worried, but he knew he had to forgive Spot. He gave his furry friend a big hug and said, "It's ok, I still love you Spot".

Spot was so happy that he started jumping up and down, and the two best friends went back to playing and having fun together.

Once upon a time there was a cute girl. She liked to listen to birds singing. One day as she was walking, she heard something calling. She stopped to listen and heard a voice that said, â€˜Help me! Help me!â€™

The girl was surprised and looked all around. Then she spotted an animal up in a tree! It was a baby squirrel in a big nest. The squirrel had gotten stuck and couldn't get down.

The girl worked hard to help the squirrel, standing on her tiptoes to reach it. Finally she got the baby squirrel free, and the squirrel hopped back up into the nest.

The girl smiled and was happy she had helped. She learned a valuable lesson that day - that if you help others, you can make them happy.

One day, Betty and her dog Boo went for a walk. Betty had a bag with her, and Boo was very curious about what was inside. 

Betty smiled as she opened the bag and brought out a teaspoons. "Wow!" said Boo. "What are these for?" 

"We're going to have a matching game!" said Betty. "We have to try and match the spoons, like lining them up in two sets of the same shape."

Boo was very excited and both Betty and Boo started to try and match the teaspoons. They worked together and soon they had matched all their spoons! 

Betty and Boo both celebrated their victory. "You were really friendly helping me match the teaspoons," said Betty. 

"That's what friends are for!" said Boo. 

The two of them continued on with their walk, both feeling very proud of what they had achieved.

Jane was very excited as she was seeing the sunrise. She was alone but it was still beautiful. The sky was like a smooth canvas filled with many lights. Jane jumped and twirled around in the golden rays, feeling so free and full of joy.

Suddenly, Jane heard a voice. It came from behind her.

"Hello! I am here too! Can I join you?"

Jane was surprised but delighted. She turned to see a small green creature. Smiling warmly, Jane said, "Yes, of course. Welcome".

The creature giggled and said, "Let's hug". Jane laughed and gave the creature a big hug.

"Thank you," said the creature. "That felt warm and soft. The light was also very nice today".

Jane smiled and nodded. "Yes, it's very peaceful. Let's keep hugging until the sun goes away!" 

So they stayed there in the bright morning light, holding each other for a long time. Jane felt happy and filled with love. It was the smoothest thing she had ever experienced. 

When it was time to go, the creature said goodbye and ran away. Jane waved with a smile on her face and thought, "I'm so lucky to have new friends."

Once there was a little dog named Jack. He was so little and helpless, he could only crawl around. One day, Jack decided to explore the world around him. He started to climb up the stairs, but suddenly he saw something strange in the corner - a big pile of spaghetti! He just couldn't resist trying it.

Jack started crawling closer and he could smell the delicious spaghetti. He was about to eat it when suddenly he heard a voice: "No, Jack! You can't eat this spaghetti!" It was Jack's mommy. She had found him trying to eat spaghetti and she knew he was too little to do it on his own.

Jack was so embarrassed and he crawled away, feeling so helpless. His mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, Jack. I'll make you your own plate of spaghetti for dinner later. You can have it then!" Jack was so happy and he crawled away to find something else to do.

Tommy said, "Hi, Jessica and Margaret! What are you doing up here?"

Jessica said, "We're roasting berries! See the fire? We put the berries in the fire and that makes them sweet. Try one!"

Tommy tried a berry. It was so yummy! He sat down and they all roasted berries together. They watched the fire burn and laughed as the berries got softer and sweeter. It was so much fun!

Once there was an ant who wanted to be powerful. He asked all of the animals in the forest how he could be powerful. A fox told him that he could act. The ant asked the fox what he meant by act. The fox said, "Acting is when you pretend to be something else but you don't really change."

The ant was excited. He decided to try it out. He pretended to be a lion. He widened his eyes, put his hands on his hips, and roared like a lion. All of the animals were scared. The ant was proud that he made them all scared.

"I am powerful!" the ant exclaimed. He continued to act like a lion and strutted around the forest. All of the animals kept their distance. The ant was very proud of himself and laughed and smiled.

He had learned that by acting, he could be powerful. He was so happy that he decided to act like a lion every day. Whenever he got scared, he acted like a lion and all the animals in the forest were scared too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sunny. Sunny was very obedient and always did what her mommy and daddy said. One day, her mommy and daddy told her they were going on a special trip. Sunny was very excited and hoped it would be a lot of fun.

When they arrived, they saw a big gun. Sunny was scared at first, but her mommy told her it was okay. She said the gun was only for protection. Sunny believed her and wasn't scared anymore.

On the way home, Sunny told her mommy and daddy that she was thankful for the gun. She said it made her feel safe. Her mommy and daddy smiled and gave her a big hug.

They were proud that Sunny was so obedient, and that she could believe in them. From then on, Sunny felt very safe whenever they went on trips. It was a happy ending!

Once upon a time there was a green field. On the green field, there was a player. The player was very happy and she thanked the beautiful day.

Suddenly, a three year old child came running on the green field. She waved at the player and said, "Hi! Can I join the game?"

The player smiled and said, "Of course! I'm so happy you're here!" She gave the child a friendly pat on the back and said, "Let's start!"

The player and the child laughed and cheered as they ran and played on the green field. After a long time, the player said, "It's time for me to go."

The child was sad but she thanked the player for the fun day. The player smiled and said, "You're very welcome! I'm so glad I got to play with you." Then, she waved goodbye and left.

The child watched her go and waved goodbye until she was out of sight. She smiled, thankful for the beautiful day they had just spent together.

Once there was a little girl called Kelly who was very adventurous. She loved to play in the garden and collect colorful rocks that sparkled like jewelry. One day, her mum put on her jewelry and teased her, saying "Oh wow, look at all the rocks Kelly has, why don't you have any jewelry like that?"

The little girl was so excited she ran outside and searched all around for the best rocks she could find. After some time, she noticed a beautiful sparkly one that seemed special. She took it inside and lay it onto the table, asking her mum if it was like her jewelry.

Her mum smiled and said yes. Kelly was so excited and asked if she could keep it. Her mum said of course, but warned Kelly not to lose it. The rock was so special, Kelly promised she'd never let it out of her sight.

From that day onwards, Kelly kept her eye on the rock. Whenever she was in the garden, she'd always take it out with her. Eventually, Kelly had enough beautiful rocks to fill a box with her own special jewelry which she proudly wore. It was exactly like her mum's jewelry and Kelly was very happy. She was glad that she was so adventurous and looked for so many rocks.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very happy with her life, and she liked to wear pink clothes.

One day, the little girl was playing with her friends. She saw a big, pink flower in the garden. She wanted to pick it, so she went over to take it. 

Suddenly, a big voice came from behind her. "Hey! That's my flower. Don't pick it!" the voice said. 

It was the big cat. The girl was sad and her face began to scrunch up. Hot tears filled her eyes, and started flowing down her face. She began to cry. 

The big cat's face changed, and he said, "Hey now, don't cry. You can pick that flower. It's okay."

The little girl smiled through her tears and wiped her face. She thanked the big cat and carefully picked the flower. 

The little girl and the big cat became friends, and from then on she always asked permission before picking any flowers. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Benny. He was only three years old, but he was very curious. He wanted to know why things were the way they were.

One day, Benny went outside and found a patch of wet grass. He asked his father why it was so wet. His father told him it was because of the rain. Benny asked his father if he could make it stop raining. His father said, "No, Benny, that's not something we can do."

Benny was a little bit sad but he thanked his father for telling him about the rain. Then he asked his father why people were so modest. His father explained that modesty was a way of showing respect and being polite. Benny thought about this for a minute and then said, "But why do we need to be polite?" His father smiled at him and told him, "Because it's the nice thing to do."

Benny nodded and smiled. He thanked his father again and they went inside the house to have a snack. Benny was thankful that his Father had told him these things. He was sure he was going to learn a lot more by the time he got to be five.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl, who liked to go on trips. She would go to the park, the beach and other fun places, but her favourite place of all was the zoo. The zoo was important to her and she went every day.

One day, the girl went to the zoo and wanted to examine the animals very closely. She tried to look at the monkeys, elephants and tigers, but the zookeeper told her to stay away. The zookeeper said it was too dangerous for her to look too closely.

The girl was determined to find another way to see the animals. She looked around the zoo until she found a way to get closer to the animals without being too dangerous. She found a way to look in at the animals from afar, so she could examine them safely.

The girl was happy. She was able to examine the animals carefully, without stepping too close. She learned a lot that day and it was an important trip for her.

One day, Mommy decided to take Susie to the park. Susie was very excited! She put on her shirt, shoes, and hat and ran outside with Mommy.

When they got to the park, they saw lots of people playing. Mommy said, "Susie, you can play over there, but remember to stay close to me."

Susie thanked Mommy and ran off to the playground. She saw some boys playing with a ball. She asked them if she could join, but they said no. Susie was sad.

But then Mommy called Susie over. She said, "Susie, it's OK. I will permit you to play with them." Susie was happy and ran to the boys. The boys said she could join, but at one point, the ball bounced and rolled into a dirty bush. 

The boys were scared to go in! But Susie was brave. She reached into the bush and found the ball. She came out holding the ball with a huge smile on her face. The boys thanked Susie, and they all continued playing. 

At the end of the day, Mommy and Susie said goodbye to the boys and went home. Susie was very happy; she had a great day!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who wanted to explore the world around him. One day, he came across an old hut and wanted to explore inside. But when he tried to push the door open, it was locked. He looked around, but couldn't find the key anywhere.

The boy sighed and was about to give up when he heard a voice from a nearby tree. The voice said: "Are you looking for the key? I have the key. You can have it in exchange for a hug!"

The boy was a bit wary at first but decided to accept the offer. He stepped forward and gave the voice a hug. As soon as he did, the voice revealed itself to be an old sparrow. The sparrow gave him the key and said: "Go ahead and explore the hut. I'm sure you'll find something interesting inside!"

The boy thanked the sparrow and used the key to unlock the door of the hut. After a few moments of exploring inside, he found a beautiful old desk that was covered in dust. He was amazed by his find, and smiled as he closed the door and locked it again with the key. He was sure he would come back to explore the hut again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was being tucked into bed by her mom. Every night, the mom would show her a sweet hug and kiss before she said good night and turned off the light.

One night, the little girl couldn't sleep. She was having a nightmare, and it was making her scared. Her mom came in to check on her and noticed that she was shaking and didn't feel very warm.

So, Mom got in bed with the little girl and showed her a hug that made the little girl feel safe. She started to feel warm and the nightmare went away. Eventually, the little girl drifted off to sleep, feeling secure and warm all night long.

Charles was anxious to explore outside. He looked out of his window and saw an interesting garage. He wondered what was inside.

Charles put on his shoes and ran outside to observe the garage. He approached the garage door, but it was locked. No matter how hard he tried, it wouldn't budge.

Charles stepped back to look around. Suddenly, he noticed a key hidden beneath the doormat. He took the key and inserted it into the door lock. It opened!

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was always looking for his favourite toy. Jack's mum was always telling him to be quiet but he was so loud.

One afternoon, Jack went looking around the house to find his toy. He searched every room but he couldn't find it. As he carried on looking, he heard something funny coming from the living room.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mimi. She was very excited because her mom told her it was time to eat. Her mom had made her favorite food - rice! With a big smile, Mimi opened her lunch box and began to eat.

But suddenly, Mimi stopped. She remembered that she had to go to school now. She was very upset and started to cry.

Mimi's mom smiled and said: "Don't worry sweetie, you can finish it later. Let me remind you when you come home. Ok?"

Mimi nodded and wiped away her tears. With a smile, she hugged her mom goodbye and left for school.

When Mimi came home, her mom reminded her: "Hey Mimi, don't forget to eat your rice!"

Mimi gave her mom a big hug and thanked her. She was no longer upset and finished her rice with a happy smile.

Once there was a little girl named Jill. She loved to explore and find fun things. One day she was playing in the garden and came across a funny knob. She twisted and twisted the knob, not knowing what it would do.

So, Jill twisted the knob and the hose began spraying water all over the yard! She laughed and ran around, playing in the wet grass. Her mom laughed too and declared that it was the funnest day ever!
